messages:
Evan: Quick heads-up: we're standardizing CI auth patterns across orgs. Goal: replace org-level PATs/service accounts and legacy Jira automation tokens with a GitHub App + per-workflow OIDC approach and fine-grained app tokens for Jira. Pilot starts 2024-10-01; org enforcement (deny legacy tokens for CI/Jira automation) on 2024-12-01. Migration guide: https://go/redwood/ci-authn-2024 :spiral_calendar:

Priya: Is the GitHub App mandatory, or can teams keep using GH Actions with OIDC only?

Evan: Teams can choose either: 1) GitHub App installation for repo-level integrations (recommended for outbound automation and webhooks), or 2) OIDC per-workflow for short-lived credentials. The key is no static org PATs for automation.

Jordan: How about our Jira bots that create tickets from CI? They use old basic-auth tokens.

Evan: Jira automation should migrate to the new Jira OAuth app we published (supporting fine-grained scopes) or use ephemeral tokens fetched via Vault. There's a migration checklist in the guide.

ops-bot: Repo discovery run scheduled: 2024-10-05 07:00 UTC. Will open issues on repos with detected legacy creds and create suggested PRs where applicable.

Priya: Will there be an automated PR generator or a compatibility shim? We have 120 repos and limited bandwidth.

Evan: Infra will ship a PR generator that can insert a compatibility shim using `actions/setup-github-app` or `vault-agent` lookups. The shim runs in a feature-flagged mode so owners can opt-in and test before we flip enforcement. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-infra/ci-authn-shims

Jordan: Any impact to self-hosted runners or Dedicated/Private installs? We run runners that need to call internal APIs.

Evan: Self-hosted runners keep host creds for provisioning, but any workflow-level calls must use OIDC or App tokens. For Dedicated/Private customers, we'll provide operator docs and a runnable sample for private networks. We'll not auto-enforce on fully customer-managed infra without agreement.

DocsBot: New docs landing: https://go/redwood/docs/ci-authn (includes sample workflows, App setup walkthrough, Jira migration, and rollback steps).

SRE-Team: We'd like 2-week windows to test critical repos. Can we whitelist service accounts temporarily?

Evan: Yes — exception process via #eng-security with tag `ci-authn-exception`. Exceptions are short-lived (max 60 days) and require compensating controls. We plan office hours next Wed/Thu to help teams.

Priya: Thanks. Can you add a short FAQ for integrators and external partners?

Evan: Will do. TL;DR: move off legacy PATs/basic tokens -> adopt GitHub App or per-workflow OIDC + Jira OAuth app or Vault ephemeral creds. Pilot Oct 1; enforcement Dec 1. Ping me or #eng-platform with repo links for priority help.
